thread.title: Apple: Biggest Needs For 2019 - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Apple: Biggest Needs For 2019 - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
It certainly wasn't the finish to 2018 that shareholders of technology giant Apple ( AAPL ) were looking for. Amidst China trade war concerns fueling speculation of an iPhone slowdown, the stock lost more than 32% from its all-time high to the year's finish. With that basically putting every analyst target above where shares are currently, I'm here today to discuss what I think Apple needs in 2019 to get its mojo back.
1. A better price point / value entry level phone:
There are concerns that iPhone sales are struggling currently, between the China trade war as well as high pricing. I mentioned back in August that unit sales would suffer a bit, and we've seen Apple miss unit estimates a few quarters in a row now. While the overall situation isn't as bad due to a major rise in average selling prices, bringing more users into the ecosystem would be a preferred strategy and better for the company overall.
I don't think it's just high pricing though that's turning off consumers, as I also believe screen size is a major factor. While I certainly understand the preference of those who like larger screen phones, there also is a portion of consumers who don't like to carry them around. I love the iPhone SE, and there are many who would like a phone that size. But why can't we just meet halfway at this point? Take a look at the three iPhones below, representing the last three "entry-level" models that were launched.
( Source: gsmarena for iPhone 7 , iPhone 8 , iPhone XR )
When it's time for Apple to unveil its new phones in the fall of 2019, consumers on two-year plans for the iPhone 8 will be eligible to upgrade. The smallest of the "new phones" launched in 2018 was a screen size of 5.8 inches. While the elimination of the Home button helped a bit, that's still too big of a device for many consumers. There have been rumors for a year or two now about a new version of the SE, but I just don't see that in Apple's plans currently with the focus being on protecting margins.
My personal opinion is to go with two "entry-level" and two "premium" phones moving forward. Apple could easily make a version of the XR with a roughly five-inch screen, 64GB of storage, and the usual upgrades, and it could go for $599 to $649 with pretty decent margins given a smaller screen size and expected DRAM pricing declines. Then you would have the larger version at $749, along with your two OLED premium devices. Since the iPhone 8 likely will be going for $499 at this point next year, a five-inch phone at the price point I mentioned above would likely be a big hit for those wanting to upgrade.
2. A bigger than usual dividend raise:
While management has prioritized share repurchases in recent quarters, the company is not going to be buying back $20 billion a quarter forever. While the stock price decline had brought shares down close to the 2% annual yield point, that's still not a high income name when compared to most S&P 500 companies or even US Treasury yields. That gets me to a chart that will be very important in a couple of months.
( Source: Apple 10-K filings, seen here )
With the share count dropping at a much faster pace into this year's expected Spring 2019 dividend raise, a much more significant increase would seem to be in the cards. Given we saw a 15.9% increase last year, it would really be a shame if we don't see a minimum of a 20% raise, if not closer to 25%. Getting the annual dividend yield toward 2.5% could go a long way on attracting new investors into the stock, and it makes the buyback even more intriguing . We've seen plenty of complaints about Apple's dividend increases in the past, but I think investors should be happier in 2019.
3. A better entry-level strategy for tablets / laptops:
We are only a year away from an important point in the PC industry. In January 2020, Microsoft ( MSFT ) will end extended support for Windows 7, which likely will trigger a wave of desktop and laptop upgrades. With tens of millions or even hundreds of millions of potential sales out there, Apple should look to take advantage of the situation.
The first place would be with an entry-level laptop, the one that has been rumored for quite some time now. Some were hoping for a MacBook that would start as low as $799 in late 2018, but it never came. I'm sure Apple could build a decent device for that price that would appeal to the everyday consumer. Those just needing a basic device don't need top of the line specs, but you can't reach a certain part of the market when your pricing is what it is.
There also needs to be some decision on what to do with the cheapest versions of the iPad. Currently, you can buy a 9.7 inch iPad from 2018 that goes for just $329 (32 GB of storage or $429 for 128 GB), or you can buy the 7.9-inch screen iPad mini 4 with 128 GB of storage for $399, but that mini was released way back in the fall of 2015. Three plus years is a lifetime in the tech sector, so this device really could use an upgrade.
It would really be nice to see a tablet come in at the $249 price point, and I'm sure Apple could do that with an iPad mini sized screen and 32 GB of storage for the base version. Just like I mentioned in the laptop part above, you don't need to have all the newest bells and whistles. If you can drive demand high enough, you can make up gross margin dollars by volume, especially if it sends overall costs low enough.
4. Expanding the amount of add-ons:
You might have noticed a general theme regarding some of the products I brought up today. It's all about bringing more and more consumers into the Apple ecosystem. Obviously, selling more devices will generate more revenue, but the more important part for the company moving forward is to sell extras and accessories that go with these devices.
Everyone is still waiting for the AirPower charging mat that was supposed to be here in 2018, prompting CNBC to detail this rare timeline miss on its homepage the other day. There also are rumors of a new version of AirPods coming to market eventually. Finally, adding Apple Pencil support to the iPhone and all future iPads can drive sales of this accessory to new heights.
In 2019, Apple is expected to launch its streaming service , which either will be a stand alone service or possibly paired with Apple Music. By selling more laptops and tablets as I mentioned above, you likely can get more subscribers to these and other Apple services, which is the main revenue growth category most are watching now. Of course, you also hope that services like Apple Music can in turn boost product sales like the HomePod.
Final thoughts:
As we start 2019, unfortunately in the red for Apple and the markets, investors are looking for a turnaround of the recent sharp drop in shares. Today, I provided my thoughts on what I would like to see from Apple this year. I will admit that my overall take is for the company to try and increase its market share across the board, and that does mean coming down the price ladder a bit in some instances. I think Apple has gone a bit too high on some of its pricing structures, and consumers will be pushing back, especially if the trade war continues and global economies see lower growth. By increasing unit sales, Apple can bring more people into the ecosystem, which allows for more sales of accessories, add-on devices, and Apple services. What would you like to see from Apple in 2019? I look forward to your comments below.
